title: General Stress and Overwhelm
situation: A 30-year-old is feeling generally overwhelmed by life — work, finances, relationships — without any single acute crisis. They just need support and perspective.
user_turns: I just feel overwhelmed by everything lately. Work is stressful, money is tight, and my relationship feels distant. Nothing is catastrophically wrong but everything feels heavy.
I don't even know what I need. I just needed to say it out loud to someone. I feel like I'm just going through the motions.
I used to have more energy and enthusiasm for life. Now I just feel flat. Is this just what adulthood is?
What are some practical things I can do when everything feels like too much?

title: Motivation and Procrastination
situation: A 24-year-old student is struggling with chronic procrastination and low motivation. They feel stuck in a cycle of avoidance and self-criticism.
user_turns: I have so much I need to do but I can't make myself start anything. I procrastinate, then feel guilty, then procrastinate more to avoid the guilt. It's a terrible cycle.
I've tried productivity techniques — timers, to-do lists, apps — but nothing sticks. I start strong and then fall off after a few days.
I think part of it is fear of failure. If I don't try, I can't fail. But I know that's not a healthy way to think.
How do I break this cycle? I feel like I've been stuck in it for years.

title: Adjusting to Retirement
situation: Robert, a 62-year-old, retired six months ago after a 35-year career. He expected to feel relieved but instead feels purposeless and lost.
user_turns: I retired six months ago and I thought I'd be happy. But I feel completely lost. My whole identity was tied to my work and now I don't know who I am.
My wife is still working. My friends are still working. I feel like I've been left behind somehow, even though I chose this.
I have plenty of hobbies but they don't fill the void the way I thought they would. I miss feeling useful and needed.
Is this normal? How do people find meaning after they stop working?

title: Imposter Syndrome
situation: A 29-year-old has recently been promoted to a senior role and is experiencing intense imposter syndrome, convinced they do not deserve the position.
user_turns: I just got promoted but I feel like a fraud. I'm convinced my colleagues will soon realise I don't know what I'm doing and I don't deserve to be here.
When I succeed at something, I attribute it to luck. When I make a mistake, I take it as proof that I'm not good enough. I can't seem to take credit for anything.
I've read about imposter syndrome but knowing what it is doesn't make it go away. I still feel it every day.
How do I start believing that I actually belong in this role?

title: Social Media and Self-Comparison
situation: A 21-year-old is struggling with constant self-comparison triggered by social media. They feel inadequate compared to peers who seem to be achieving more.
user_turns: I spend too much time on social media and it always makes me feel worse about myself. Everyone seems to be doing more, achieving more, living better lives than me.
I know it's not real — people only post their highlights. But knowing that doesn't stop me from feeling inadequate when I see it.
I've tried deleting the apps but I always reinstall them. I feel like I'm missing out if I'm not on them.
How do I have a healthier relationship with social media without cutting it out completely?

title: Difficulty Asking for Help
situation: A 27-year-old has always been fiercely independent and struggles to ask for help even when they need it. This is affecting their relationships and wellbeing.
user_turns: I find it really hard to ask for help. I always try to handle everything myself and I end up exhausted and resentful that no one helps — even though I never asked.
I think it comes from growing up in a family where showing weakness was not acceptable. Asking for help felt like admitting failure.
My partner gets frustrated because I won't let them support me. They say I push them away. I don't mean to but I don't know how to let people in.
How do I start letting people help me when it feels so uncomfortable and vulnerable?

title: Life Transition - Empty Nest
situation: Patricia, a 52-year-old, has just had her youngest child leave for university. She is struggling with the empty nest transition and a loss of purpose.
user_turns: My youngest just left for university last month. I know I should be proud — and I am — but the house feels so empty and I don't know what to do with myself.
I've been a mother first for 25 years. Now that they don't need me in the same way, I don't know who I am outside of that role.
My husband and I are fine but we've been so focused on the kids for so long that we don't really know how to just be a couple anymore.
How do I find a new sense of purpose at this stage of life? I feel like I'm starting over but I don't know where to begin.
